title: Batch B architecture read is blocked by cross-wave comparison drift
symptom: Wave 2 Batch B completed with trusted package truth, but comparison against the trusted Batch A package is not defensible because the graph epoch changed and the expanded cross-DLL seeded surface shows large apparent verified-count drops on previously trusted DLLs.
smallest_reproducer: Compare trusted Batch A campaign 538f7e84 against trusted Batch B campaign 53575f28 on the same lane/profile. Batch B adds contoso_events.dll and contoso_cs_interwoven.dll, changes graph_epoch, and shows workflow/reporting/pricing drops under cross-DLL seeding.
trust_impact: Next-system selection is untrustworthy because apparent frontier change may be caused by uncontrolled comparison variables rather than real architecture shift.
allowed_next_actions: audit wave-to-wave comparability using graph_epoch, seeding_mode, and package composition
reduce the issue to the smallest trustworthy 6-DLL or 8-DLL comparison boundary
fix or explicitly model graph epoch and cross-DLL seeding for package-wave comparisons
rerun Batch B only after the comparison surface is controlled
disallowed_next_actions: select the next architecture tranche from Batch B as-is
treat the Batch B family ranking as authoritative without fixing comparability
exit_criteria: wave-to-wave package comparison uses an authoritative comparable surface
apparent regressions on the prior trusted Batch A slice are either explained or eliminated
Batch B can be compared to its baseline without graph-epoch or cross-DLL hidden-variable ambiguity
